title: Slack for designers on Mac, with Lazur: shortcuts, huddles and canvases in 2026
metaTitle: Slack for Designers on Mac: Shortcuts, Huddles and Canvases
description: Slack for designers on Mac: the desktop shortcuts, huddle steps, canvas and Figma setup that matter, plus how Lazur helps you while you work.
secondaryKeywords: Slack Mac screen sharing not working
intro: Slack for designers on Mac means the desktop app, set up around projects, threads and huddles. Use ⌘ G to search, ⌘ ⇧ H to start a huddle, and a canvas for decisions that need to last. Lazur can point at the right button and answer out loud while you work.
tldr: Install the Mac desktop app and keep one install, since switching copies can break screen sharing.
Learn ⌘ G, ⌘ F and ⌘ ⇧ H first, because Slack does not currently allow custom shortcuts.
Free workspaces keep 90 days of history, so save final decisions in a canvas or a pinned message.
Lazur points at buttons and answers out loud while you hold ⌥ ⌘, but it never clicks for you.

blocks.text: Most designers do not need a complicated Slack setup. You need three things: channels that match your projects, a fast way to find old feedback, and a clear rule for when a huddle beats a message. This guide covers those in the order you will use them each day.
Install the Mac app and check your version

Use the desktop app for daily work. The browser tab works, but the Mac app keeps notifications, keyboard shortcuts and huddles in one window. It also stays open while you move between Figma, Photoshop and your files.

Slack's recent Mac builds, from October 29 to November 9, 2026, are security and maintenance releases. The latest is 4.53.283. None of the three notes mention menu or interface changes, so the steps in this guide should still match your screen.
Pick one install and avoid screen-share failures

Some people move from the direct download of Slack to the Mac App Store version. Huddle screen sharing can then fail, even when System Settings shows Slack as allowed. Slack's help page lists this as a known bug in the Mac desktop app.
Choose one install and keep it. If you already switched, the fixes are in the screen sharing section near the end of this guide. Try the fixes before a client call, not during one.
Keyboard shortcuts designers use most

Slack's shortcuts are fixed. The help center says custom keyboard shortcuts are not currently possible. Learn the defaults you use most, and skip the rest. These five save the most time in design work.

items: ⌘ G starts a search across your workspace.
⌘ F searches inside the conversation you have open.
⌘ B bolds text, and ⌘ I italicizes it. Use them to mark up feedback lists.
⌘ ⇧ H starts, joins, leaves or ends a huddle.

blocks.text: Check the full set on Slack's keyboard shortcuts page before you build habits around one key. Shortcuts can change with a Slack update. The page is the reference that counts.
Set up channels for each project
Make one channel for each active project. A channel named after the project beats a general design channel. You search by project name, and people remember names faster than topics.

Example. A checkout redesign gets its own channel. The PM, the engineers and the designer post there. The weekly review notes go in a pinned message, along with the Figma link. Anyone who joins later finds everything in one place.
Mute the channels you only check once a week. Muting keeps them from pulling your attention during focus time. The mute guide covers the steps and the difference between muting and hiding a channel.
Save final decisions outside the chat. A decision buried in a long thread is hard to find a month later. Pin it, save it for later, or put it in a canvas.

blocks.title: Free plans forget
blocks.text: Free workspaces keep only the most recent 90 days of message and file history. Slack began deleting messages and files more than one year old on August 26, 2024. Copy any decision you may need later to a canvas or a pinned message.
Give feedback in threads, not the main channel
Threads keep a review in one place. Replies stay attached to the post they answer. The main channel stays readable for everyone else, including people who only check in on Fridays.

Start with a short post that names the screen and the decision. For example: Checkout step, two button labels, need a call by Thursday. Then give your notes in the thread. Reviewers answer under the same post, so the decision is easy to trace.

Search finds old comments fast. Press ⌘ F inside a conversation to find a word in that channel. Press ⌘ G to search the whole workspace when you remember a phrase but not the place. The Threads view collects the threads you follow.
Start a huddle for a live design critique

A huddle is a quick voice call inside Slack. To start one on desktop, click the headphones icon in the conversation header. The huddle window lets you turn on video and add people. The arrow next to the headphones icon copies the link.
Use ⌘ ⇧ H when your hands are on the keyboard. The same shortcut starts, joins, leaves or ends a huddle, so you can use it in both directions.

Plan the group size before you start. On a free plan, a huddle has a maximum of two participants. On a paid plan, up to 50 people can join, but only 25 can turn on video at a time. A critique with six people needs a paid plan.

A good critique huddle has a host, one shared screen and a written list. Share the frame during the call, take notes in a thread, then post the decisions in the channel afterward. The call ends fast, and the record stays.
Use canvases for decisions that should last

A canvas is a shared document inside Slack. Use one for a design brief, a decision log or a review checklist. To create one on desktop, go to Home > Files in the sidebar, click the plus button at top right, and select Canvas.

You can also add a canvas as a tab in a channel or DM. Click the plus sign in the conversation header, select Canvas, then click Insert and Share. The document then sits next to the conversation that uses it.

Set access on purpose. Owners and people with edit access can change and comment. View-only people can ask the owner for Edit Access or Comment Only Access on desktop. The mobile app does not support that request, so send new reviewers to a laptop.

blocks.title: Check your plan
blocks.text: Slack's canvas help page says canvases are available on paid plans, and Frontline Members cannot create them. On a free workspace, keep decisions in a pinned message until you can use a canvas.
Get Figma updates in Slack without the noise
Figma can post file updates into Slack through the Figma app. Invite it to a channel with /invite @figma. Then run /figma subscribe to pick a file, a folder or a team.

Choose the update frequency with care. Real time posts every change. Hourly and daily options batch the changes. Daily updates can arrive at a set delivery time, which suits a team that works in one time zone.

Example. A team with a few active files sets a daily update for each file, not a real time feed. The channel shows one clear summary each morning. Reviewers ask for a closer look only when a change matters.
Mind the app cap. Free workspaces can install 10 third-party or custom apps. The Figma app is a third-party app, so it takes one of those slots. Remove an app you no longer use before you add it.
Read unread messages without losing your place
Designers often come back from a focus block to a long channel. Jump to the latest unread message first, then work down. Use the Unreads view to see everything that changed since you last looked.

Mark a message as unread when you need it back at the top of your list. Mark all messages as read only when you truly want a clean slate. These two moves are different, and mixing them up makes people miss feedback.
Why Slack pulls you out of your work

Slack's own research says 68% of respondents spend at least 30 minutes a day toggling between tools. Over half, 56%, say switching between apps makes it harder to get essential work done. The survey covered 17,000 knowledge workers.

Treat that as vendor research. Slack ran the survey, and the page does not give a survey year. The point still holds for designers. Each switch costs attention, so batch your Slack time instead of checking it all day.
Mistakes designers make in Slack on Mac

items: Posting feedback in a DM. Only one person sees it, and the next designer cannot find it.
Leaving every channel on full notifications. Mute the channels you only skim.
Assuming history lasts. Free workspaces keep 90 days of message and file history.
Planning a six-person critique on a free plan. A free huddle allows two participants.
Mixing the App Store and direct download copies of Slack, which can break screen sharing.
Hunting for custom shortcuts. Slack does not currently support them, so learn the defaults.

blocks.text: Fix screen sharing and notifications when they break

If huddle screen sharing fails on your Mac, Slack's help page lists three fixes. Remove Slack under Screen & System Audio Recording in System Settings, then open Slack again. Or run tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.tinyspeck.slackmacgap in Terminal. Or reinstall the direct download.
Run the fixes from least disruptive to most. Restart Slack after each change. Then test with a short huddle before you rely on screen sharing in a client call.

If messages stop alerting you, the problem is often a notification setting, not the app. Start with the [notification fix guide](/how-to/fix-missing-notifications-in-slack). Then pause notifications during focus time with the [pause guide](/how-to/pause-notifications-in-slack).
Where Lazur helps in Slack on your Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch. It is not a plugin or add-in for Slack, and it does not click buttons or operate Slack for you. It sees your screen, then helps you find things and understand them.

Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. That helps when a feedback reply runs long and typing it out takes too long. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.
Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. The trial needs no credit card and starts when you first open the app. Current plan prices are on the [pricing page](/pricing).
If you want the design-focused version, see [Lazur for designers](/for/designers). It covers voice help in Figma, Photoshop and Slack.
Next steps for a cleaner Slack week

items: Create one channel for your current project with [How to create a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/create-a-channel-in-slack).
Find old comments with [How to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack).
Practice thread replies with [How to reply in a thread in Slack on Mac](/how-to/reply-in-a-thread-in-slack).
Protect focus time with [How to pause notifications in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pause-notifications-in-slack).
Try Lazur for voice help in any app from the [download page](/download).

faq.question: Is there a Slack app for Mac, or do I have to use the browser?
faq.answer: Slack has a desktop app for Mac. It keeps notifications, keyboard shortcuts and huddles in one window. You can also use Slack in a browser, but this guide assumes the desktop app. Slack's release notes list 4.53.283 as the latest Mac build.

faq.question: Can I change the Slack keyboard shortcuts on Mac?
faq.answer: No, not currently. Slack's help center says it is not possible to set custom keyboard shortcuts. Learn the defaults instead, such as ⌘ G for search and ⌘ ⇧ H for huddles.

faq.question: How much message history does a free Slack workspace keep?
faq.answer: Free workspaces keep the most recent 90 days of message and file history. Slack began deleting messages and files more than one year old from free workspaces starting August 26, 2024. Save any decision you may need later.

faq.question: Why does screen sharing fail in a Slack huddle on my Mac?
faq.answer: Slack's help page lists a known bug for people who moved from the direct download app to the Mac App Store version. Remove Slack under Screen & System Audio Recording, run the tccutil reset command in Terminal, or reinstall the direct download.

faq.question: How many people can join a Slack huddle?
faq.answer: On a free plan, a huddle has a maximum of two participants. On paid plans, up to 50 people can join, but only 25 can turn on video at one time.

faq.question: Can a Figma file post updates into Slack on its own?
faq.answer: Yes. Invite the Figma app with /invite @figma, then run /figma subscribe and pick a file, folder or team. You choose real time, hourly or daily updates. Daily updates can arrive at a set delivery time.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Slack?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Slack. It works in any app on your Mac while you hold the shortcut. It can point at buttons, answer questions and guide you one click at a time. It does not click for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my Slack messages all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Is Lazur available on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, but it is not available. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
